ImageDescription.value:
Chair-O-Plane at the Send, Münster, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
The Send is Münster’s big folk festival and takes place three times a year on Schlossplatz square. Its origins date back to the 9th century. The name is derived from the Middle Low German word “Synode”, meaning church assembly. In the Middle Ages, this synod was combined with a market, which over time developed into an annual fair.
Today, the Send is one of the largest folk festivals in the Münsterland region. Fairground rides, stalls, music, and fireworks characterize the event and attract hundreds of thousands of visitors.
A historical symbol is the Send sword at the historic town hall. This sword was formerly erected during the Send as a sign of market peace. It stood for protection, legal certainty, and special order during the market. Even today, the Send sword commemorates the medieval roots of the festival and combines tradition with lively folk culture.

Artist.value: Dietmar Rabich

ImageDescription.value:
Canoes on the coast, Tsitsikamma National Park, Eastern Cape, South Africa
Tsitsikamma National Park is located on the famous Garden Route in the Eastern Cape province. It was established in 1964 and was one of Africa’s first marine national parks. Today, it is part of the larger Garden Route National Park.
The name “Tsitsikamma” comes from the Khoikhoi language and means “place with plenty of water”. The park protects an impressive coastal landscape with steep cliffs, dense evergreen forests, and a species-rich marine area.
The suspension bridges at the mouth of the Storms River are famous for their spectacular views of the Indian Ocean. In addition to coastal and marine conservation, the park also includes parts of the original Afro-montane forest with large yellowwood trees.
